row.evidence: Short.io's SSO guide says "SSO is available on the Enterprise Plan" and that it "automatically creates a SAML-based login ... for each user who logs in via SSO for the first time"; no SCIM is documented on any plan.
row.notes: Status unchanged (none): SAML SSO with JIT account creation on Enterprise only; no SCIM endpoint in the docs index or API reference (JIT-only, may be reclassified at merge). Changes since June: the tier table is now Free $0, Hobby $5/mo, Pro $18/mo, Team $48/mo, Enterprise $148/mo (annual: $50, $180, $480, $1,480 per year, 'SAVE 17%'); June's 'Personal: $20/mo' team plan no longer exists and Free/Hobby/Pro are 1-user plans, so the team plan is now Team. Enterprise $148/mo matches June. Pricing is flat per account, not per user, so per-user fields are null. The public REST API manages links, domains and statistics only (it can grant link-level permissions to a userId) and has no user or team endpoints.

plans.name: Hobby
plans.notes: 1 user; annual price shown with the Annual toggle.

audit_log_api.notes: An in-app audit log (Settings > Audit) exists; no audit-log API endpoint is listed.

rate_limits.text: API rate limit 50 req/s on every plan (link API, not user management).

user_api.notes: The developers.short.io reference (llms.txt index) lists link, domain, folder, QR, targeting and statistics endpoints only; no user, member or team endpoints. Link-level permissions take a userId (POST /links/permissions/{domainId}/{linkId}/{userId}) but do not manage users.

okta.notes: Vendor guide sets up a custom SAML 2.0 app via Create App Integration; okta.com/integrations/short-io/ returned 404, so no OIN listing found.

entra.notes: Vendor guide uses a non-gallery app.

google.notes: Vendor guide for Google Workspace SAML.

fallbacks.other_sync: Default role for new SSO members via a SAML attribute (Admin, User, Readonly, Restricted)
